intensive therapy in type 1 diabetic patients reduces the risk of development and progression of retinopathy and microalbuminuria and that intensive therapy in the DCCT cohort reduces the incidence and progression of coronary artery disease.

intensive glycemic control in individuals with type 1 or type 2 diabetes can delay or prevent the onset or slow the progression of diabetic complications and, in individuals with type I diabetes, that this benefit is sustained for at least 20 years after treatment cessation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the long-term effects of intensive diabetes management on complications and the natural history of diabetes and its complications in a population with type 1 or type 2 diabetes.
understanding the mechanisms of diabetes and its complications, the impact of diabetes therapies and other interventions, and the prevention and treatment of diabetes complications.

the following: 1) understanding the mechanisms by which intensive therapy reduces the risk of long-term diabetes complications; 2) determining the effects of intensive treatment on the natural history of type 1 disease, including its progression to insulin independence; 3) evaluating the long-term effects of intensive therapy and its impact on health-related quality of life; and 4) identifying and characterizing the risk factors for diabetes complications and other adverse outcomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DCCT/ EDIC is a unique and valuable resource for the scientific and clinical community and has provided a wealth of information about the natural history of type 1 diabetic complications.
the DCCT/ EDIC has been a landmark clinical trial in the history of diabetes research.
intensive therapy is the standard of care in the management of type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the benefits of intensive glycemic control are long-lasting and include the prevention of retinopathy, nephropathy, and neuropathy.

the DCCT/ EDIC has provided the strongest evidence to date that intensive glycemic control can prevent or delay the onset and progression not only of microvascular complications but also of the macrovascular complications of type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
intensive therapy is associated with a 50% reduction in microvascular complications and a 40% reduction in the risk of cardiovascular disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
intensive therapy reduces the risk of microvascular complications and that the benefits of intensive therapy persist for at least 30 years.
the benefits of intensive glycemic control in type 1 diabetic individuals are long-lasting and extend well beyond the original DCCT follow-up.
type 1 diabetes is a treatable condition, and that the earlier and more intensively it is managed, the better the outcomes.
